title: Who Committed the 1912 Villisca Ax Murders?
summary: Josh and Chuck examine the June 1912 Villisca, Iowa ax murders, in which eight people (the Moore family and two overnight guests, the Stillinger sisters) were killed in their home. They cover the discovery, the contamination of the crime scene by townspeople, the local suspects (Frank Jones, William Blackie Mansfield, and the traveling preacher George Kelly, who was tried twice and acquitted), and the modern serial killer theory linking Villisca to axe murders in Colorado Springs, Mammoth (Illinois), Ellsworth and Paola (Kansas), and Columbia, Missouri, with Henry Lee Moore considered and largely dismissed. The episode closes with a listener mail story about hookworm and sign-off.

segments.title: Intro and Villisca town hall call
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode, joke about the number of 'X murders', call the Villisca town hall to settle pronunciation, and note the grisly subject matter and sources such as Mike Dash's Smithsonian article and Ed Epperly's research.

segments.title: Background and the Moore household
segments.summary: Location of Villisca in southeast Iowa, the Moore family and the overnight guests the Stillinger sisters after a children's day service, and the household settling in for the night.

segments.title: The murders
segments.summary: The killer entered the unlocked house after midnight with Joe Moore's ax, used an oil lamp, and killed the parents and children in their sleep with the blunt side, then struck the victims many times with the sharp side and covered mirrors and faces.

segments.title: Discovery and contaminated crime scene
segments.summary: The killer left before dawn; neighbor Mary Peckham noticed the house was quiet; Ross Moore found the bodies and Marshal Hank Horton was called. Doctors, a minister, a coroner and townspeople entered, contaminating the scene; a train town with bloodhound searches found no suspect.

segments.title: Suspect Frank Jones and Blackie Mansfield
segments.summary: State senator and businessman Frank Jones was suspected due to his rivalry with Joe Moore over a farm equipment business and an alleged affair with his daughter-in-law. Detective James Wilkerson then suspected William Blackie Mansfield, who had an alibi and was exonerated.

segments.title: George Kelly trial and confession
segments.summary: Traveling preacher George Kelly, an Englishman with a reputation for lewd conduct, was suspected; he had been in town, and there were claims of a witness and a confession later recanted. He was tried twice; the first jury was split and the second acquitted him.

segments.title: Serial killer theory and related axe murders
segments.summary: Modern researchers link Villisca to axe murders in Colorado Springs, Mammoth, Ellsworth, Paola and Columbia, Missouri, with shared traits such as bent-wick oil lamps and covered mirrors. Henry Lee Moore is discussed and considered a red herring; the Paola witness and the Colorado Springs neighbor attack are described.

segments.title: Closing remarks and listener mail
segments.summary: Hosts wrap up with references to further reading and a listener email from James in St. Pete, Florida, about hookworm symptoms, followed by the sign-off and contact information.
